subject: health
unitTitle: Sexual Health, Disease Prevention, and Community Action
title: Application or project: consent and coercion
essentialQuestion: How can understanding sexual health, disease prevention, and community action help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Coercion uses pressure, threats, manipulation, or power to override choice; consent is absent when agreement is not informed, freely given, current, and reversible.
A safe communication plan states the limit clearly, recognizes pressure or danger, identifies an exit, and brings in adult or professional support when direct engagement is unsafe.
For consent and coercion, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Complete a fact-checked community-health project with family review choices, private questions, and no disclosure requirement.
studentTask: Annotate a supplied fictional exchange about consent and coercion: underline the stated limit, circle any pressure or respectful check-in, and write a two-sentence response that states a boundary plus a safe next step. Add when a trusted adult should enter the plan.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in consent and coercion; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
